root_cause.text: The `klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer` function in the `kl5kusb105` USB serial driver triggers a slab out-of-bounds write because it passes the full buffer size to `kfifo_out_locked` without reducing the copy count by the header length reserved at the start of the buffer.
root_cause.evidence: The patch modifies the `kfifo_out_locked` call argument from `size` to `size - KLSI_HDR_LEN`, and the CVE description explicitly states that "When the fifo holds at least size bytes, size bytes are copied starting two bytes into the size-byte buffer, writing KLSI_HDR_LEN bytes past its end," which matches the KASAN report noting the buggy address is "2 bytes inside of allocated 64-byte region."

vuln_statements.explanation: Based on the vulnerability root cause, the klsi_105_prepare_write_buffer function passes the full buffer size (len) to kfifo_out_locked without subtracting the header length reserved at the start of the buffer. This causes a slab out-of-bounds write because the copy operation writes more data than intended into the buffer space, exceeding the allocated memory boundary.
